I've been working this land for six years now, and I know what this ground in Quzhou can do. Most of my 66 mu goes into the wheat-maize rotation — that's the backbone of my income and what feeds my family. I'll put 58 mu into that rotation. I've got 5 mu of stevia under contract with a local processing company, which pays better per mu than grain, and 3 mu of sweet potato, mostly for home use and the local market.

For wheat this winter, I'll plough before sowing — I want a clean seedbed after last year's maize stubble. I'll use the improved Jimai variety that the extension station recommends and apply base fertilizer with a decent nitrogen top-dress at jointing. Three irrigations: pre-sowing, jointing, heading. Two pesticide runs — herbicide early and a fungicide before heading for powdery mildew.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll go straight into summer maize with no-till direct seeding to save time and moisture. I'll use hybrid seed, split my nitrogen between sowing and topdress at the big bell stage. Two irrigations should be enough if summer rain is decent.

The stevia I manage carefully — it's my best cash earner per mu and the processing company wants clean leaf, so I keep disease pressure down. The sweet potato I handle traditionally, heavy on potassium, light work overall.
